Dustwallow Marsh (or Dustwallow Swamp) is a vast and ancient swamp in the eastern reaches of Central Kalimdor. Although there is little activity in the area, the Alliance and the Horde have recently expanded their influence in the region. The Alliance city-state of Theramore was located on a small island east off shore but was eventually destroyed by a mana bomb ordered by the then-Warchief Garrosh Hellscream. The Horde major stronghold in the area is Brackenwall Village, the new home of the ogre Stonemaul clan.
In earlier years, scattered reports of black whelps spotted in the southern region sent hunters rushing to claim Stormwind's bounty. Few ever succeeded in locating one of Onyxia's lost brood. Now, few who enter this marsh wish to be found, let alone trifled with. There are many scattered refugees of the Second War who are unable to find hearth or kin in a kinder climate. Though roadways connect dry stretches of land to coastal vistas, few beyond the occasional fisherman have risked such paths since the destruction of Theramore.

Although there is little activity in the area, the [[Alliance]] and the [[Horde]] have recently expanded their influence in the region. The Alliance [[city-state]] of [[Theramore (nation)|Theramore]] was located on a [[Theramore Isle|small island]] east off shore but was eventually destroyed by a [[mana bomb]] ordered by the then-Warchief [[Garrosh Hellscream]]. The Horde major stronghold in the area is [[Brackenwall Village]], the new home of the [[ogre]] [[Stonemaul clan]]. In earlier years, scattered reports of black whelps spotted in the southern region sent hunters rushing to claim [[Stormwind (kingdom)|Stormwind]]'s bounty. Few ever succeeded in locating one of [[Onyxia]]'s lost brood. Now, few who enter this marsh wish to be found, let alone trifled with. There are many scattered [[refugee]]s of the [[Second War]] who are unable to find hearth or kin in a kinder climate. Though roadways connect dry stretches of land to coastal vistas, few beyond the occasional fisherman have risked such paths since the destruction of Theramore.{{Ref WoWCodex|116}} ==History== [[File:DustwallowComic.jpg|thumb|Dustwallow Marsh.]] ===Third War=== {{WC3-section}} Dustwallow Marsh had long been home only to wild beasts, but all this changed in the [[Third War]], when [[Jaina Proudmoore]] led her people here to settle down after the battle with [[Archimonde]] at [[Mount Hyjal]].[[To Tame a Land]] Founding the [[city-state]] of [[Theramore (nation)|Theramore]], Jaina's people rapidly extended into the swamp, building fortified [[scout tower]]s at important points along the road to the [[Barrens]]. The area was home to the [[centaur]] and [[wildkin]] who raided orc members. [[Bloodbeak the Berserker]] destroyed an orc village here. After [[Daelin Proudmoore]] attacked the [[Echo Isles]], [[Vol'jin]] relocated his tribe to the marsh. His base served as a base of operations for [[Rexxar]], [[Rokhan]], and [[Chen Stormstout]]. The [[mok'nathal]] recruited the [[ogre]]s of [[Stonemaul clan]] that lived here into the [[Horde]] when he killed their tyrannical leader [[Kor'gall]]. Dustwallow Marsh saw a great skirmish between the Horde and [[Kul Tiras (kingdom)|Kul Tirans]] led by Admiral Proudmoore, eventually leading to Daelin's death and the permanent breakup of the tentative peace between the [[Alliance]] and the [[Horde]].[[Old Hatreds]][[A Blaze of Glory]] ===World of Warcraft=== {{wow-section}} Perhaps it is because of extreme terrain conditions that neither the [[Horde]] nor the [[Alliance]] has succeeded in establishing an extensive presence in the area. Though it is shown that several orc families live here.''[[World of Warcraft: The Comic]]'' Located on the rocky tip of the peninsula on the eastern shore, the citadel of [[Theramore Isle]] is the home of [[Jaina Proudmoore]] and a great bastion of the Alliance. The gleaming walls of this bastion, however, often serve to contain the Alliance, and its presence does not extend far beyond them, despite a number of scattered checkpoints and towers that dot the road leading to the [[Barrens]]. Theramore's military has recently been dwindling, partly due to the ever-increasing number of desertions, though why so many people have chosen to forsake their place with the Theramore garrison remains a mystery. Despite bordering on Horde-controlled territory, [[tauren]] and [[orc]]ish presence in Dustwallow Marsh is equally marginal and is largely confined to [[Brackenwall Village]] to the northwest. Founded by the Stonemaul ogres and ruled by the iron fist of their leader, [[Overlord Mok'Morokk]], Brackenwall Village is the only vestige of the Horde in the area. As the Stonemaul ogres do not generally seem to take much interest in the outside world, much of the area between the bastion of Theramore Isle and the Horde settlement remains wild and untamed, with even the road leading to the Barrens rapidly falling into disrepair. Though neither faction controls a significant portion of Dustwallow Marsh, covert skirmishes between the Alliance and Horde became common, in spite of the official truce that was maintained in the region. There have been reports of Brackenwall Village taking military action against the covert Theramore infiltrators, who have been spotted to the east of the village. Other sources indicate that a number of Horde spies have been murdered or simply disappeared while attempting to infiltrate Theramore. Clandestine activities on both sides continue to this day and are more likely to escalate into a full-fledged covert conflict than cease completely. In the south of the marsh, the [[black dragonflight]] has established a presence. Consequently, these regions of the swamp have come to be known as the [[Dragonmurk]] and the [[Wyrmbog]]. Until recently, the Stonemaul ogres lived in [[Stonemaul Ruins|Stonemaul Village]] in this region in relative peace. The [[Mok'Nathal]] [[Rexxar]] assumed leadership of their tribe some time ago and forged an alliance between the Stonemaul and the Horde, although later it seems he stepped down as a leader. Not long after, the Black Dragonspawn attacked the village in a terrible rout and the surviving Stonemaul ogres were forced to retreat to Brackenwall but the ogres have sworn revenge on the usurpers. It is said that this wilderness is also home to [[Onyxia]], a great black dragon and the daughter of [[Deathwing]], and even some adventurers ventured into her lair and lived to tell the tale. At this time, the [[Theramore Guard]] was still seeking the exact location of Brackenwall, its [[Theramore Infiltrator|infiltrators]] doing their best to find it.[[The Missing Diplomat (15)]] ===The Burning Crusade=== {{bc-section}} The goblins of the [[Steamwheedle Cartel]] created the town of [[Mudsprocket]] in the southwest of Dustwallow Marsh. At the same time, the [[Grimtotem tribe]] expanded their influence in the region by settling in the northern reaches founding [[Blackhoof Village]]. ===Cataclysm=== {{cata-section}} Dustwallow Marsh was almost entirely untouched by the [[Cataclysm (event)|Shattering]]. The only changes of note were a new road from Theramore directly to the [[Southern Barrens]] and a new mountain pass from [[Mudsprocket]] to [[Thousand Needles]]. ===Mists of Pandaria=== {{mop-section}} The relative quiet didn't last long though. After [[Deathwing]]'s fall, Theramore was attacked and [[Attack on Theramore Isle|destroyed]] by a [[mana bomb]] detonated under the orders of [[Garrosh Hellscream]], then-[[Warchief]] of the Horde. Once Garrosh Hellscream was defeated and captured in the [[Siege of Orgrimmar]], [[Varian Wrynn|King Varian Wrynn]] stated that he wanted to set up a garrison close to Theramore. ===Legion=== {{Legion-section}} During the [[third invasion of the Burning Legion]], [[Dr. Weavil]], having survived his previous encounter, called upon gnomes for an internship on [[Alcaz Island]]. The gnomes flocked to the island but were infected, becoming drudge gnomes. Anti-aircraft artillery, mines, and mechanical spiders were put to protect him and his nefarious plans. [[Clint]] was the only known gnome to escape from Weavil's grasp and warned adventurers trying to infiltrate the isle.[[Return to Alcaz Isle]] ===Battle for Azeroth=== {{Bfa-section}} During the [[Fourth War]], the [[Theramore Isle|Ruins of Theramore]] saw some activity in the form of scouting missions as well as being a place of meetings. Adventuring jewelcrafters discovered a [[Jewelhammer's Vault|forgotten vault]] beneath Alcaz Island.[[The Missing Chapter (quest)]] Prior to the [[battle at the Gates of Orgrimmar]], a Horde army loyal to [[Varok Saurfang]] made a camp at the site of a watch tower. There, leaders of the Horde gathered and met with [[Anduin Wrynn|King Anduin]]. Together, they marched on Durotar and the city of Orgrimmar. ===Dragonflight=== {{Df-section}} The [[Sullied Banner]] claimed the Ruins of Theramore, where they created [[mana bomb]]s on [[Theramore Isle]] to protect themselves from their enemies. They were thwarted by the [[blue dragonflight]] and under the order of [[Kalecgos]] ceased their activities. ===The War Within=== {{Tww-section}} After [[Magni Bronzebeard]] attempted to commune with [[Azeroth]], the [[Radiant Song]] manifested magical anomalies and displaced creatures across Dustwallow Marsh. ==Geography== [[File:Alcaz Island.jpg|thumb|Alcaz Island.]] Dustwallow Marsh is a dense, humid thicket filled with a perpetual fog and weathered hovels. A hot, fetid swampland in [[Central Kalimdor]], Dustwallow Marsh is home to a variety of predators, including [[raptor]]s, [[spider]]s, [[crocolisk]]s, and [[murloc]]s. [[Black dragon]]s dwell in the southern end of the swamp. Dustwallow Marsh abuts the ocean on its east side; off the coast there are some islands like [[Alcaz Island]], or a rocky island on which was perched the Alliance stronghold-city of [[Theramore Isle|Theramore]] until it was destroyed by [[Warchief]] [[Garrosh Hellscream]]. Near the low hills that form the western edge of the Marsh separating it from the Barrens, the [[Stonemaul clan|Stonemaul]] [[ogre]]s have opened their [[Brackenwall Village]] to the races of the Horde. Brackenwall serves as an essential foothold for the Horde in the marshlands. ===Maps and subregions=== [[File:VZ-Dustwallow Marsh-t1.jpg|thumb|left|Map of Dustwallow Marsh after Theramore's destruction.]] [[File:VZ-Dustwallow Marsh.jpg|thumb|left|Map of Dustwallow Marsh before Theramore's destruction.]] {| class="darktable hlist" |- | *[[Alcaz Island]] **[[Jewelhammer's Vault]] *[[Blackhoof Village]] *[[Bloodfen Burrow]] *[[Bluefen]] *[[Brackenwall Village]] *[[Darkmist Cavern]] *[[Dragonmurk|The Dragonmurk]] **[[Den of Flame|The Den of Flame]] **[[Stonemaul Ruins]] *[[Dreadmurk Shore]] *[[Dustwallow Bay]] **[[Nat's Landing]] **[[Tidefury Cove]] *[[Great Sea|The Great Sea]] *[[Lost Point]] *[[Mudsprocket]] *[[North Point Tower]] *[[Quagmire|The Quagmire]] **[[Beezil's Wreck]] **[[Direhorn Post]] **[[Tabetha's Farm]] *[[Sentry Point]] *[[Shady Rest Inn]] *[[Theramore Isle]] **[[Foothold Citadel]] *[[Witch Hill]] **[[Swamplight Manor]] *[[Wyrmbog]] **[[Emberstrife's Den]] **[[Onyxia's Lair]] |- || ---- ;[[Undisplayed location]]s *''[[Bleeding Sparrow]]'' *[[Theramore Highway]] |- || ---- ;Removed locations *[[Ironclad Prison]] *[[Moggle Point]] *[[West Point Tower]] |- || ---- ;[[Lore location]]s *[[Demonsbane Inn and Tavern]] |- || ---- ;{{WC3FT-inline}} [[Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne|Warcraft III]] *[[Coastal Base]] *[[Den of the Lost]] *[[Dustwallow Keys]] *[[Goblin Library]] *[[Magic Shop]] *[[Magistrates Temple]] *[[Tomb of the Ancients (Warcraft III)|Tomb of the Ancients]] |- || ---- ;{{RPG-inline}} [[Warcraft RPG]] *[[Bluefen#In the RPG|Bluefen Village]] *[[Brackenwall]] *[[Broken Giant|The Broken Giant]] *[[Ironclad Prison#In the RPG|Ironclad Prison]] *[[Shady Rest]] |} VZ-Dustwallow Marsh-old2.jpg|Map of Dustwallow Marsh prior to ''[[World of Warcraft: Cataclysm|Cataclysm]]''. At Brackenwall Village, [[Overlord Mok'Morokk]] seeks aid in the battle against the black dragonflight. In her cottage in the Quagmire, [[Tabetha]] recruits the arcanely inclined in an attempt to cleanse the taint that has affected a mystical orb. In his lair, [[Emberstrife]] unwittingly helps disguised agents of the Horde in entering his queen's lair, and at Theramore Isle, Lady [[Jaina Proudmoore]] sends bold adventurers into the swamp in search of a missing diplomat. [[Nat Pagle]] also resides at [[Nat's Landing]], where adventurers from around the world come to hear of his fishing adventures and from where he offers guidance to those who have significantly advanced the patient art. ==Quests== [[File:Shady Rest.jpg|thumb|Shady Rest Inn]] {{main|Dustwallow Marsh storyline}} Adventures aid their respective factions by dealing with spies, investigating the [[Shady Rest Inn]] and [[Grimtotem tribe|dealing with the culprits]], and striking out against the [[Black dragonflight]]. ==Resources== [[File:Darkmist Cavern.jpg|thumb|Darkmist Cavern]] * [[Herb]]s ** [[Stranglekelp]] ** [[Kingsblood]] ** [[Liferoot]] ** [[Fadeleaf]] ** [[Goldthorn]] ** [[Khadgar's Whisker]] ** [[Bogbean Plant]] * [[Leather]] ** [[Thick Murloc Scale]] (Drops off level 30-35 [[murloc]]s) ** [[Turtle Scale]] (Skinning level 38-53 [[turtle]]s) * [[Ore]] ** [[Silver Ore]] ** [[Iron Ore]] ** [[Gold Ore]] ** [[Mithril Ore]] ** [[Truesilver Ore]] ==Wild creatures== * {{RaceIcon|BogBeast}} [[Bog beast]]s * {{RaceIcon|Crocolisk}} [[Crocolisk]]s * {{RaceIcon|Frog}} [[Frog]]s * {{RaceIcon|SpiderGiant}} [[Giant spider]]s * {{RaceIcon|Hydra}} [[Hydra]] * {{RaceIcon|Ooze}} [[Ooze]]s * {{RaceIcon|Raptor}} [[Raptor]]s * {{RaceIcon|Shark}} [[Shark]]s * {{RaceIcon|SpiritWolf}} [[Spirit wolf|Spirit wolves]] * {{RaceIcon|Snake}} [[Snake]]s * {{RaceIcon|Threshadon}} [[Threshadon]]s * {{RaceIcon|Turtle}} [[Turtle]]s * {{Race|Undead}} ** {{RaceIcon|Ghost}} [[Ghost]]s ** {{RaceIcon|Zombie}} [[Zombie]]s * {{RaceIcon|WindSerpent}} [[Wind serpent]]s * {{RaceIcon|Worm}} [[Worm]]s ==In World of Warcraft== ===The Burning Crusade=== {{bc-section}} In [[patch 2.3.0]], the whole zone of Dustwallow Marsh was improved to make it more quest-friendly and a less lonely place to be in. Changes included: * A new neutral town, [[Mudsprocket]], led by [[Steamwheedle Cartel]] goblins. After completing the {{Alliance}}[[Theramore's Fall (Alliance)|Theramore's Fall]]/{{Horde}}[[Theramore's Fall (Horde)|Theramore's Fall]] scenario, Theramore is replaced with a crater, making all quests in it unavailable. Players can ask [[Zidormi]] near the bridge to switch back to the zone's original [[Phasing|phase]], restoring Theramore and allowing questing. ==In Warcraft III== [[File:WC3x-O02-04.jpg|thumb|Loading screen from ''Warcraft III''.]] [[File:Dustwallow Marsh Map.jpg|thumb|In-game map from ''Warcraft III''.]] {{WC3-section}} {{QuoteWiki|Deep within the marshes of Dustwallow, the Stonemaul ogres have crafted a crude village. Though the ogres were once allied with the orcs, they have grown to hate the smaller race and are no longer willing to lend them aid. It is strength alone that the ogres value now.|[[Old Hatreds (WC3 Orc)|Old Hatreds]] Dustwallow Marsh loading screen.}} In ''[[Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne]]'', Dustwallow Marsh was the main map of the [[Old Hatreds (WC3 Orc)|Old Hatreds]] mission of the [[Founding of Durotar]] campaign. It is there that the [[Darkspear tribe]] trolls resettled after the [[Echo Isles]] were attacked by the [[Kul Tiras (kingdom)|Kul Tiran]] navy. Besides the Darkspear village, it featured some orcish and troll outposts, such as [[Mathogg]]'s village. The zone had a human [[Coastal Base]] nearby, close to [[Theramore Isle#In Warcraft III|Theramore Isle]] and [[Tidefury Cove#In Warcraft III|Tidefury Cove]]. [[Mulgore#In Warcraft III|Mulgore]] could also be accessed through a [[zeppelin]] ride, the [[Stonemaul clan]] ogres had a [[Stonemaul Village|village]] and an [[arena]] south, and there was a [[dimensional gateway]] to the [[Outland Arena]]. Dustwallow Marsh then had some wildlife which didn't appear later in ''World of Warcraft'': *{{RaceIcon|Air}} [[Air elemental]]s *[[Arachnathid]] *{{Race|Bronze dragonflight}} *{{Race|Centaur}} *{{RaceIcon|Earth}} [[Earth elemental]]s *{{Race|Demon}}s (mostly within the [[Magistrates Temple]] and around the portal to the [[Outland Arena]]) *{{RaceIcon|Golem}} [[Golem]]s *{{Race|Harpy|[[Harpy|Harpies]]}} *{{RaceIcon|Wendigo}} [[Jungle Stalker (Warcraft III)|Jungle stalkers]] *{{Race|Kobold}}s *{{RaceIcon|Murloc}} [[Mur'gul]] ([[Den of the Lost]] only) *{{Race|Naga}} (mostly within the [[Coastal Base]] area) *{{Race|Quilboar}} *[[Revenant]]s (and the [[Eldritch Deathlord]]) *{{RaceIcon|ThunderLizard}} [[Salamander]]s ([[Tomb of the Ancients (Warcraft III)|Tomb of the Ancients]] only) *{{RaceIcon|Wendigo}} [[Sasquatch]] *{{RaceIcon|SpiderCrab}} [[Spider crab]]s *{{RaceIcon|ThunderLizard}} [[Thunder lizard]]s *{{RaceIcon|Water}} [[Water elemental]]s *{{Race|Wendigo}} (Den of the Lost only) *{{Race|Wildkin}} It also had the following dungeons: [[Tomb of the Ancients (Warcraft III)|Tomb of the Ancients]], [[Magistrates Temple]], [[Den of the Lost]], and some uninstanced monster areas such as a [[centaur]] fort, an [[hydromancer]]'s island, a Kul Tiran outpost led by [[Captain Thornby]], a kobold [[gold mine]] and a bronze dragon's lair. The unnamed [[Stonemaul Village|Stonemaul village]] was its own sub-map. The tribe's [[Ogre mage|ogre magi]] and [[priest]]s lived in the upper part of the settlement and maintained their own [[Magic Shop]]. The village was also home to a grand ogre [[arena]] and a Gauntlet valley filled with powerful monsters, including a large [[quilboar]] community led by a giant [[Razormane Chieftain]], [[jungle stalker]]s and [[sasquatch]] living together, as well as giant [[thunder lizard]]s and [[wildkin]]. Old Hatreds - Stonemaul - Razormane Chieftain.jpg|Quilboar in the Gauntlet valley. ==In the RPG== {{RPG-section}} ===History=== Dustwallow Marsh was once a high plain filled with herd animals that thrived on the tall grasses. Then came the [[Great Sundering|great Sundering]], and the plain was smashed down into a sundered valley. The water table bled up into the ruined landscape, creating the great marsh that exists today.''[[Warcraft: The Roleplaying Game]]'', pg. 198 ===Geography=== Dustwallow is a temperate to hot watery swamp. Dustwallow Marsh is located southeast of the Barrens and north of Thousand Needles. The swamp curls to the east, forming a bay around the island of Theramore. Dustwallow is a flood plain fed by underground springs and surrounded by the dry savannas of the [[Barrens]]. The marsh is eternally wet, muddy, and hot, unfit for proper settlements and a haven for creatures that crave the wetness and humidity. Narrow banks of slippery mud separate endless stagnant pools and algae-choked channels, making Dustwallow a traveler’s nightmare. The roads that cross the fen are muddy and treacherous, and the surrounding swamp is even more dangerous to traverse. Those who mistake the thick, wandering bogs of the marsh for solid land may fall through, only to have the floating plants close above and trap them in the brackish water. Dustwallow teems with predators that lurk just beneath the surface of every pool and skulk behind every bush. In the east, the turbid water of the marsh mixes with salt water from the sea. The rocky form of [[Theramore Isle]] lies just beyond in the bay. The marsh is the best way to approach Theramore by land, as jagged rocks outside the bay make sailing directly from the goblin city of [[Ratchet]] difficult. The marsh’s southern expanse grows rockier as it approaches [[Thousand Needles]]. The pools are larger and far deeper, with half-submerged rocky outcrops. Many of these rock clusters have openings that lead into cave systems. The caves are often surprisingly dry and serve as lairs for a variety of beasts. Some conjecture exists whether the caves are interconnected with the underground river that keeps the swamp submerged or if they might even extend out to the sea. ===Inhabitants=== The hundreds of shallow pools that comprise the marsh hold creatures ranging from massive plant eating kodo beasts to ambushing packs of raptors to territorial water-loving murlocs. The saltwater swamp of east Dustwallow is a popular breeding area for the murloc packs. Indeed, the waters teem with aquatic creatures of all sorts. Humans and murlocs drag nets down the channels to harvest gigantic mudfish, but also pull in everything from [[alligator]]s to eels. Poisonous snakes hang from the trees, and some of the larger specimens are known to drag the unwary up into the branches. Of course, these dangers are nothing compared to those of Dustwallow’s southern region. The rocky outcroppings common to this area are ideal lairs for black dragons, and those creatures are so common in the area that it has earned the name "Wyrmbog". ==Notes and trivia== *The trees of Dustwallow were considered to be "marshy garbage" by the sailors and shipwrights of [[Theramore Isle|Theramore]], who were jealous of the [[orc]]s' access to good oaks from [[Azshara|the mountains]] above [[Orgrimmar]].''[[Cycle of Hatred]]'', chapter 1 *It should also be noted that the zombies and spirits that haunt the areas of Witch Hill and Swamplight Manor do not appear linked to the Scourge or the Lich King but may be the sole work of the demon [[Zelfrax]] who is summoned and defeated at the end of the quest chain [[Cleansing Witch Hill]]. *The raid dungeon [[Onyxia's Lair]] and the micro dungeon [[Alcaz Island]] can be found in this area. No other dungeons or battlegrounds are located here. *This area was planned to be available in the [[Southern Barrens warfront]]. ==Speculation== {{Speculation}} In ''[[Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne|The Frozen Throne]]'', the distinctions between Dustwallow Marsh, the [[Barrens]] and [[Durotar]] are blurry. Even though the level [[Old Hatreds (WC3 Orc)|Old Hatreds]] is said to take place in Dustwallow, it includes a land path to [[Orgrimmar]] (although Rexxar travels to [[Vol'jin]]'s camp on a zeppelin from Orgrimmar to the Barrens at first). Regional borders and the locations of settlements were evidently changed around with the release of ''[[World of Warcraft]]''. As such, many of Dustwallow's locations such as the Darkspear camp and its denizens may have been [[retcon]]ned to be somewhere else. Alternatively, the camp may have been abandoned and or destroyed. ==Gallery== File:Stonemaul Ruins.jpg|Stonemaul Ruins. File:Brackenwall Village.jpg|Brackenwall Village.
